method: Whole-file manual reading of three installer/solution definitions; pinned bytes verified and two XML documents parsed.
findings: MSI is per-machine with embedded compressed cabinet, main executable and conditional context-menu, desktop-shortcut and system-PATH components. These declarations do not prove install, repair, rollback or uninstall behavior.

Major upgrade schedules afterInstallInitialize. Alternate upgrade-code range detects/removes other release channel. LegacyUninstall invokes installed executable deferred without impersonation and ignores return status; its completion is not an installer success gate.

Option preservation uses existing shortcut/context registry searches and a substring test for WinDirStat in system PATH, rather than exact normalized path membership. Actual migration cases remain unqualified.
Directory context command quotes executable and selected directory; Drive command quotes executable but leaves percent1 unquoted. No runtime argument-parsing counterexample established.
Desktop shortcut component uses HKCU registry key path in a per-machine package; multi-user repair and ownership behavior require Windows installer tests.

Store manifest template declares Windows FullTrustApplication and runFullTrust, with architecture/version/device-minimum placeholders and26 language resource entries. It does not declare installer-equivalent shell/PATH components here.

Solution has six named debug/release platform combinations, but Debug ARM64 maps to Release ARM64. A Debug ARM64 solution invocation therefore does not establish debug assertions or debug runtime for that platform.
limits: XML well-formedness is not WiX/AppX schema, compilation, signing, installation, upgrade or runtime qualification.
No scripts or installers executed, no foreign production code adopted; native pHash investigation deferred. Global completed repository count remains147/500.
